input: Buy and learn to use a Dutch oven for camping

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether 'learn to use' means mastering a few basic recipes vs. full campfire cooking proficiency changes how deep and broad the learning plan needs to be.
Dutch ovens range from ~$30 to $400+; budget directly determines which models to recommend (e.g., Lodge camp vs. premium enameled cast iron).
Cooking method differs significantly between open campfire, charcoal briquettes, or camp stove, and affects which oven style and size to buy.
Group size determines the right oven capacity — a solo camper needs a 2-qt, while a family or group needs an 8–12 qt model.
Target dishes (e.g., stews, bread, cobblers, whole chicken) influence both the size of oven to buy and which techniques to prioritize learning first.
Whether success means completing a first cook on an upcoming trip vs. building long-term skill shapes the urgency and structure of the plan.
Knowing if the user has cooked outdoors before or used cast iron at home determines how much foundational instruction to include vs. jumping straight to camp techniques.

gold.taskTitle: Buy and learn Dutch oven camping cooking
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to purchase a Dutch oven suitable for camping and develop the skills to cook with it outdoors.

questions.title: What meals do you most want to cook in it?
questions.description: Identify the target dishes (e.g., stews, sourdough bread, cobblers, roasts) to determine which techniques to learn first and what oven features matter most.

questions.title: What is your budget for the Dutch oven?
questions.description: Establish a price range to narrow recommendations — entry-level bare cast iron (~$30–60), mid-range (~$60–120), or premium enamel-coated ($150–400+).

questions.title: How many people will you typically be cooking for?
questions.description: Group size is the primary driver of oven capacity — solo/couple (2–4 qt), small group (6 qt), or large group (10–12 qt).

questions.title: What heat source will you use at camp — fire, charcoal, or stove?
questions.description: Open campfire, measured charcoal briquettes, or a camp stove each require a different oven style (legs vs. flat bottom) and different temperature-control techniques.

questions.title: Do you have any experience with cast iron or outdoor cooking?
questions.description: Prior familiarity with seasoning, heat management, and camp cooking determines how much foundational guidance to include in the learning plan.

questions.title: Is there a specific camping trip you are preparing for?
questions.description: A fixed upcoming trip creates a hard deadline that shapes urgency — which skills to prioritize and whether to do a practice cook at home first.

questions.title: How deep do you want to take your Dutch oven skills?
questions.description: Clarifies scope — whether the goal is one or two reliable go-to recipes, or a broader repertoire covering multiple techniques like baking, braising, and frying.
